clinicalPearls: Intermediate-grade, rarely metastasising mesenchymal neoplasm of myofibroblastic and fibroblastic spindle cells set within an inflammatory infiltrate of plasma cells, lymphocytes and eosinophils.
Predominantly affects children and young adults; the lung, mesentery, omentum, retroperitoneum and genitourinary tract are characteristic sites.
Around half harbour ALK gene rearrangements at 2p23 with aberrant ALK protein expression on immunohistochemistry.
ALK-negative tumours may instead be driven by ROS1, NTRK, RET or PDGFRB fusions, so a negative ALK result does not exclude the diagnosis.
May present with a paraneoplastic inflammatory syndrome — fever, weight loss, anaemia, thrombocytosis and raised inflammatory markers — that regresses after complete excision.
Complete surgical resection is the cornerstone of treatment and is usually curative for localised disease.
Targeted ALK inhibition (for example crizotinib) is effective for unresectable, recurrent or metastatic ALK-positive disease.
Epithelioid inflammatory myofibroblastic sarcoma is an aggressive variant, typically carrying a RANBP2-ALK fusion with a nuclear-membrane ALK staining pattern.
reference.pathophysiology: Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour is a clonal neoplasm of myofibroblastic and fibroblastic spindle cells accompanied by a prominent reactive infiltrate of plasma cells, lymphocytes and eosinophils within a variably myxoid, vascular or densely collagenous stroma. In roughly half of cases the driver is a rearrangement of the ALK receptor tyrosine kinase gene on chromosome 2p23, which fuses ALK to a partner gene and produces constitutive kinase activation with aberrant cytoplasmic ALK expression; the fusion partner influences the staining pattern, and in the epithelioid sarcomatous variant a RANBP2-ALK fusion produces a distinctive nuclear-membrane pattern with more aggressive behaviour. ALK-negative tumours may instead be driven by fusions involving ROS1, NTRK, RET or PDGFRB, so the unifying theme is aberrant tyrosine kinase signalling. The accompanying inflammatory cells and their cytokine milieu, including interleukin-6, are thought to underlie the constitutional features — fever, anaemia, thrombocytosis, raised inflammatory markers and polyclonal hypergammaglobulinaemia — that resolve once the tumour is removed. Behaviour is usually that of a locally recurring lesion with only rare distant spread, although abdominal and extrapulmonary sites recur more readily and the epithelioid variant behaves aggressively.
additionalInvestigations: Contrast-enhanced CT or MRI to define tumour extent and resectability
Core or excisional biopsy with histopathological assessment of the spindle cell and inflammatory components
Immunohistochemistry panel including ALK, smooth muscle actin and desmin
Molecular testing for ALK rearrangement by FISH or sequencing and, if negative, for ROS1, NTRK and RET fusions
Full blood count and inflammatory markers to document the paraneoplastic inflammatory picture
PET-CT for staging when aggressive or epithelioid features are present
redFlags: Epithelioid morphology with a nuclear-membrane ALK pattern, indicating the aggressive sarcomatous variant
Rapid enlargement, necrosis, marked cytological atypia or multifocal disease
Persistence or recurrence of constitutional symptoms after resection, suggesting residual or recurrent tumour
Involvement of critical thoracic or abdominal structures precluding complete excision
reference.prognosis: Localised tumours treated by complete resection have an excellent outlook, though local recurrence is common at abdominal and extrapulmonary sites. Distant metastasis is rare overall, but the epithelioid variant behaves aggressively and advanced ALK-positive disease often responds to targeted inhibitors.
pitfalls: Mislabelling the lesion as a high-grade sarcoma or dismissing it as a purely reactive inflammatory process
Assuming ALK negativity excludes the diagnosis when other kinase fusions may be responsible
Overlooking the option of ALK-directed therapy in unresectable or metastatic disease
Confusing it with IgG4-related disease when plasma cells are abundant
